curation_rationale: Statin-induced feedback can increase cholesterol-synthesis gene expression; matches the cholesterol/fatty-acid program.
Sterol synthesis blockade can induce compensatory sterol-regulated genes, consistent with the positive response.
Experimental repression of cholesterol/SREBP genes in HepG2 cells is consistent with the negative lipid-program response; context dependent.
Glucocorticoid class regulates hepatocyte transcription, coagulation proteins and bile-acid handling; plausible positive hepatobiliary-program response, not proof of all pathways being activated.
Experimental glucocorticoid effects on bile-acid synthesis/transport support a hepatobiliary pathway connection; individual processes may differ in direction.
Blocked stimulated microglial amyloid-beta phagocytosis/clearance experimentally; directionally consistent with suppression of the MGM amyloid-clearance program.
Direct mevalonate-pathway perturbation with compensatory sterol-gene transcription, consistent with a positive response.
Direct connection to cholesterol biosynthesis; positive transcriptional response is compatible with compensation, although feedback for this exact signature is inferred.
Experimental sterol-gene induction after synthesis blockade supports a positive cholesterol-program response.
Experimental cholesterol/mevalonate gene repression is consistent with a negative projected response; context dependent.
